vacc.description: The server vAcc this package belongs to, for packages that split one vAcc's airspace between them (e.g. lfxx for the French FIR packages). The client asks the server for this scope; absent, it asks for the namespace. The namespace still names the controller's profiles folder.

anyOf.description: RGB colour [r, g, b], each a whole number from 0 to 255
RGBA colour [r, g, b, a], each a whole number from 0 to 255; an alpha of 255 is opaque

color.description: RGBA colour [r, g, b, a] or [r, g, b], each a whole number from 0 to 255, the alpha too (255 is opaque). Any other value reads as absent and the package check says so.

width.description: Line width in logical pixels. Never drawn thinner than 1.

dashArray.description: Dash, gap, dash, gap and so on, in logical pixels: an even number of values, repeated along the line. An odd count repeats with dashes and gaps swapped; a value of 0 or less draws solid

type.description: The built-in symbol, a sprite, or shape for the shape named by shape. Lower case only: any other value reads as absent and the package check says so.

size.description: The dot's radius in logical pixels. 0 draws the layer's own 3 pixel dot; a negative size draws no dot.

sprite.description: Name of the sprite defined in the sprite atlas

shape.description: With type shape: the name of a shape in systems/shapes.json, drawn at each point in its own colours and design units, growing with the display scale. A feature's own symbol is drawn in its place.

fillColor.description: RGBA colour [r, g, b, a] or [r, g, b], each a whole number from 0 to 255, the alpha too (255 is opaque). Any other value reads as absent and the package check says so.

strokeColor.description: RGBA colour [r, g, b, a] or [r, g, b], each a whole number from 0 to 255, the alpha too (255 is opaque). Any other value reads as absent and the package check says so.

rotation.description: Rotation of the symbol in degrees

color.description: RGBA colour [r, g, b, a] or [r, g, b], each a whole number from 0 to 255, the alpha too (255 is opaque). Any other value reads as absent and the package check says so. The label's red, green and blue; a label is always drawn opaque. Not written: each label takes its point's colour.

fontFamily.description: The face the layer's labels draw in, in every system whose mapstyle names none: an alias of the manifest's fonts or a font the client bundles (Inter, RobotoMono). Not written: Inter. A name that is neither draws in Inter and is told once in client.log.

fontSize.description: Label size in pixels. Not written: 10, or 11 on a layer named label.

fontWeight.description: Coarse stroke weight, applied as a coverage threshold shift so no second atlas is needed. Overridden by textWeight when both are set.

textWeight.description: Fine stroke weight. Negative thins the strokes, positive thickens them, 0 is the font's own weight. Overrides fontWeight.

textSharpness.description: Edge hardness. 0 keeps the rasteriser's own antialiasing, 1 gives a near-binary edge. A negative textWeight with some sharpness gives a thin, crisp look.

lineHeight.description: Pixels from one line's baseline to the next, in the label's own size. A label breaks at each line break in its text, and at spaces with wordWrap. Not written or 0: 1.2 times the font size. A system's mapstyle layer style overrides it.

align.description: Where each line of a label sits beside the others. Not written: left. A system's mapstyle layer style overrides it.

wordWrap.description: On, a line breaks at the last space before it passes wordWrapWidth; a word wider than that stays whole. Not written: off. A system's mapstyle layer style overrides it.

wordWrapWidth.description: Pixels a line may run to while wordWrap is on, in the label's own size. Not written: 100. A system's mapstyle layer style overrides it.

scaleWithZoom.description: NOT SUPPORTED. Map labels are a constant screen size by design, and the per-size glyph atlases depend on that; zoom-scaled text would need an SDF path.

minZoom.description: The labels are hidden below this map zoom, on the scale the layer's own minimum zoom is on. Inclusive. Not written: no lower limit. A system's mapstyle layer style overrides it.

maxZoom.description: The labels are hidden above this map zoom. Inclusive. Not written: no upper limit. A system's mapstyle layer style overrides it.

padding.description: Pixels the plate reaches past the text on every side, in the label's own size. Used only where backgroundOpacity is above 0. Not written: 0. A system's mapstyle layer style overrides it.

backgroundColor.description: The colour of the plate behind the layer's labels, in every system whose mapstyle names none. backgroundOpacity multiplies its alpha; written alone, it draws at its own alpha. Not written: the map background.

backgroundOpacity.description: Above 0, a plate is drawn behind each label and over the map under it, its colour's alpha times this. Not written: 1 where backgroundColor is written, else no plate. A system's mapstyle layer style overrides it.

geodesic.description: Whether a long oblique segment is drawn as the great circle between its ends instead of the straight Mercator chord. Default true. Segments under 20 km and segments whose ends share a latitude (a parallel) are always straight. Overridable per feature with a top-level geodesic property. The server projects sector volumes with the same rule.

alias.description: The family name a tag item, a list column, a map layer's text style or a route label names to draw with this font. No space at either end and no comma or #: the client refuses such an alias, tells it once in client.log and registers nothing under it.

lastActiveProfile.description: Written by the client while the package is in use: the profile it last had open, as the main window's profile and the one on show, each a path under the package. Not an author's setting.

activeProfile.description: The profile on show, which may be the main one.

squawk.description: The package's own squawk allocation. Each system's policy still ranks or disables a provider by its name under squawk.providers.

http.description: A first-party HTTP allocator, built once for the package and offered to every system's chain: one request per code asked for, a POST with a JSON body or a GET with query parameters (method), carrying the facts named under fields; the code comes back as a JSON object or as the plain text body (response). A block that breaks a rule here is refused whole: no allocator is built, nothing is sent, and client.log names the field and the rule.

endpoint.description: Absolute https URL. Plain http is refused.

name.description: Provider name in each system's chain, and the name squawk.providers in a system's policy ranks or disables it by. Default Http.

priority.description: Declared priority. Default 50: above the server, below a plugin's 100.

timeoutSeconds.description: Seconds a request waits before the chain moves on, 1 to 60: a controller is waiting on the code. Default 5.

codeProperty.description: The response property carrying the code. Default code.

apiKeyEnvironmentVariable.description: The environment variable holding the API key, sent as a bearer token; the key never lives in the package. Only a name that starts NEORADAR_SQUAWK_ and goes on in capital letters, digits or underscores is read.

minIntervalSeconds.description: Whole seconds between the start of one request and the next, for a service that rate limits. Requests wait their turn in the order they were asked, one at a time, and read their facts when it comes. Default 0: no waiting.

method.description: POST sends the facts as a JSON body, GET as query parameters. Default POST.

response.description: json reads codeProperty of a JSON object; text takes the whole body as the code, which must be four digits from 0 to 7. Default json.

fields.description: The name the server wants each fact under, to the fact. Absent, the six facts of the flight (callsign, origin, destination, flightRule, aircraftType, cruiseLevelFt) go under their own names. A fact with no value is left out. callsign is the aircraft's; controllerCallsign is the controller asking; codesInUse is every other flight's transponder and assigned code that does not end 00, joined with ~; latitude and longitude are the aircraft's, to six places; originNearby is the origin, only while the aircraft is under 50 kt and within 3 nm of it.

plugins.description: Plugins this package offers to load when it is opened. Each entry is given either as a full path or as a path relative to the package root (e.g. "plugins/UKControllerPlugin.nrplugin"). A package ships each of its own plugins as a .nrplugin archive, which an approval covers whole: a file inside a package (this one, or any in the client's packages folder) that is not a .nrplugin is refused, because a bare .dll loads the files beside it, unless the controller has turned on "Trust package plugins and allow native library plugins" in General Settings; otherwise a .dll, .so or .dylib loads only from a full path a controller pins outside every package. An entry is an offer: it loads for a controller once they approve it in Plugin Settings, and an approved file that changes asks again; with that setting on, every entry loads when the package opens without asking. Only a plain local file path loads (on Windows a drive path with nothing after the file name): a network share, a device or NT object path (\\?\, \\.\, \??\) and an alternate stream are refused, and a relative entry must stay inside the package. A .nrplugin is referenced as the archive, never as the binary it unpacks. The client's plugin window writes full paths here, approved as it writes them; a package ships its own plugins as relative ones.

installedFiles.description: Written by the client when it installs or updates the package from a provider: each file it installed, by its path in the package, with that file's checksum. Not an author's setting.

lastOpened.description: Written by the client each time the launcher opens the package: when, as an ISO 8601 time. Not an author's setting.

altitudeFormat.description: How altitude-valued tag items render either side of the transition altitude. A system's labels.json overrides this; omit both and items using "format" fall back to the EuroScope convention (an "A" and two digits below, three above).

prefix.description: Text before the digits, e.g. "A" below the transition altitude.

suffix.description: Text after the digits, e.g. "00" to render full feet rather than hundreds.

digits.description: MINIMUM digit count of the value in hundreds of feet, zero-padded and never truncated. 2 renders 3000 as "30" and still renders 12000 as "120".

prefix.description: Text before the digits, e.g. "A" below the transition altitude.

suffix.description: Text after the digits, e.g. "00" to render full feet rather than hundreds.

digits.description: MINIMUM digit count of the value in hundreds of feet, zero-padded and never truncated. 2 renders 3000 as "30" and still renders 12000 as "120".
